sections.title: Who I am
sections.body: I'm a software developer and researcher with a background in Computer Science, experience in backend development, and a strong interest in software architecture, cloud computing, distributed systems and artificial intelligence. My work sits at the intersection of product development, academic research and hands-on exploration, building systems that balance architectural quality, performance, security and scalability.

sections.title: Education
sections.body: I hold a Bachelor's degree in Computer Science from the Federal University of Ceará (UFC), where I'm currently pursuing a Master's degree in the same field. My academic background is grounded in practical work: software development, scientific research, teaching assistance and projects of my own.

sections.title: Research
sections.body: My master's research addresses computational offloading in Mobile Cloud Computing, investigating the computational and energy impact of processing mobile workloads remotely through bidirectional gRPC communication. The work involves experimentation across mobile devices and servers, measuring energy consumption, CPU and memory usage, and communication and processing performance, alongside a comparison of different languages and offloading strategies. The goal is to clarify the trade-offs involved in moving computation from mobile devices to remote resources.

sections.title: Professional background
sections.body: I worked as a systems developer at FitBank, a company in the financial sector, primarily with C#, .NET, Angular, SQL Server, MongoDB and Azure. I contributed to building and maintaining financial systems: REST APIs, banking operations, service integration, legacy maintenance and architectural evolution, applying practices such as Clean Architecture, SOLID, Git, CI/CD and agile methodologies. I currently work in research and development at Akiyama on artificial intelligence and computer vision, including liveness detection mechanisms and applied Deep Learning models.

sections.title: Teaching
sections.body: During my undergraduate studies at UFC, I spent four semesters as a teaching assistant for Algorithms, Data Structures and Advanced Data Structures, helping students build a solid grasp of programming fundamentals and problem solving. I also tutored for the Brazilian Informatics Olympiad (OBI), coaching students in programming logic and algorithms, mostly in Java. Both roles sharpened my technical communication and mentoring skills, and deepened my own understanding of the fundamentals.
